suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-20 adds this relationship only as the user-approved bounded clinical proposition. The cited review reports that keratoconjunctivitis sicca affects up to 95% of patients with Sjögren disease and is often the earliest and most persistent manifestation, driven by autoimmune-mediated lacrimal gland dysfunction and ocular-surface inflammation. Require an established diagnosis of Sjögren's syndrome and objective evidence of dry eye disease/keratoconjunctivitis sicca (for example Schirmer testing, tear-film break-up time, or ocular surface staining) with compatible chronology; the cited review reports that keratoconjunctivitis sicca affects up to 95% of patients with Sjögren disease and is often the earliest and most persistent manifestation, driven by autoimmune-mediated lacrimal gland dysfunction, without establishing that Sjögren's syndrome caused an individual's dry eye as opposed to other causes of aqueous-deficient or evaporative dry eye. Preserve meibomian gland dysfunction, environmental and medication-related dry eye, age-related tear-film changes, contact lens wear, prior ocular surgery, and other autoimmune or ocular-surface conditions as competing explanations. Do not infer Sjögren's syndrome from dry eye symptoms alone, and do not treat this population-level association as proof that Sjögren's syndrome caused an individual's dry eye disease. The cited literature supports only this constrained proposition and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.
